posts.title: Breakfast from six, and the paper bag before it
posts.excerpt: The breakfast room opens at six because the first intercity leaves Central at ten past. For guests on that train, six is already too late, so Marta packs a paper bag.
posts.content:
The breakfast room opens at six because the first intercity leaves Central at ten past. For guests on that train, six is already too late, so Marta packs a paper bag.

It holds a coffee in a lidded cup, a warm roll with butter and cheese, a piece of fruit and a yoghurt with a spoon. Tell the desk the night before and it will be waiting from half past five, with your room number written on the side.

Why it is free

Nobody pays extra. Breakfast is part of the room price, and it seemed wrong to charge a guest twice because their meeting starts in another city at nine.

Last year Marta packed a little over four thousand bags. She says the regulars never need to ask any more; she simply knows which mornings they leave early.

posts.title: The walk from Central station, in four minutes
posts.excerpt: Most of our guests arrive by train, and most of them arrive tired. The walk from the platform should be the easiest part of their day.
posts.content:
Most of our guests arrive by train, and most of them arrive tired. The walk from the platform should be the easiest part of their day.

Leave Port Ellis Central by the harbour exit, not the main concourse. Turn right under the plane trees and follow Quay Street for two hundred and eighty metres. The hotel is the grey stone building on the left with the dusty rose door.

At night and in the rain

The pavement is flat and wide all the way, with no kerbs to lift a suitcase over. At night the street is lit and there is always someone at the desk who can see the door.

If it rains, ring the desk from the platform. We keep six large umbrellas by the door, and Daniel has been known to walk to the station with one.

posts.title: What makes a hotel desk actually work
posts.excerpt: When we rebuilt the rooms in 2022, we asked forty regular guests what they would change. Almost all of them talked about the desk.
posts.content:
When we rebuilt the rooms in 2022, we asked forty regular guests what they would change. Almost all of them talked about the desk.

So every desk is now under the window, where the daylight is, and wide enough for a laptop and a folder side by side. The chair is a real office chair with an adjustable back, not a dining chair with a cushion.

Sockets, light and wifi

There are two sockets and two USB points at desk height, and two more by the bed. The wifi is tested every Monday for video calls, and the lamp is warm enough for a camera without making you look grey.

It is not glamorous. It is simply what people who travel for work need, and it took us twenty years to notice how few hotels get it right.

posts.title: Three tables on the old quay for one person at nine
posts.excerpt: Eating alone after a long day should not feel like an imposition. The old quay is two minutes from the hotel, and these three restaurants will seat one person late without a sigh.
posts.content:
Eating alone after a long day should not feel like an imposition. The old quay is two minutes from the hotel, and these three restaurants will seat one person late without a sigh.

The fish restaurant at the end of the quay keeps a counter by the kitchen for single diners. The Italian place in the old rope store serves until half past ten and does a very good half portion of anything.

Booking from the desk

And the small wine bar under the arches has six tables, a short menu of plates to share or not, and staff who will leave you alone with a book.

The desk can book any of them for you, for one person or for a client dinner of six. Ask for the list; it changes with the seasons.

posts.title: Company accounts, without a contract
posts.excerpt: More than half our guests are sent here by their employers, many of them every week. A company account makes that simpler for everyone.
posts.content:
More than half our guests are sent here by their employers, many of them every week. A company account makes that simpler for everyone.

There is no contract and no minimum number of nights. Your company receives one invoice at the end of the month, with cost centres or project codes if it needs them, and guests do not have to keep receipts.

Regular rooms

Regular guests can ask for the same room every time, and we hold it when they book. The desk keeps a note of the things that matter: the quiet side of the building, a taxi at six, oat milk at breakfast.

To open an account, write to Helen with the company name and an invoice address. It usually takes a day.

posts.title: Rebuilding eighty-four rooms without closing
posts.excerpt: In 2022 we rebuilt every room and every bathroom in the hotel. We did it floor by floor, over eleven months, and we never closed.
posts.content:
In 2022 we rebuilt every room and every bathroom in the hotel. We did it floor by floor, over eleven months, and we never closed.

Each floor took nine weeks. The builders started at eight and stopped at five, the floor above and below stayed empty, and guests on the other floors were told on arrival and offered a different week if they preferred.

What changed

The rooms got double glazing, new beds chosen by Sofia after a week on each mattress, rain showers, desks under the windows and a little less furniture. The corner rooms became studios for longer stays.

Arthur, who opened the hotel in 1987, came to see the last floor finished. He said it finally felt like the harbour he had in mind.
